scope: LITD2 health trauma and field healing
core_rule: HP and trauma are independent systems.

families.name: Fracture
families.primary_effect: strong limb-dependent penalty and aggravation risk

families.name: Plaie profonde
families.primary_effect: effort can reactivate HP loss or bleeding

families.name: Traumatisme crânien
families.primary_effect: perception targeting or information-reading penalty without deliberate input lag

families.name: Côtes fêlées
families.primary_effect: guard effort and physical recovery penalty

families.name: Bras blessé
families.primary_effect: weapon attack or parry penalty depending on affected arm

families.name: Infection
families.primary_effect: secondary persistent degradation such as max HP or recovery penalty

families.name: Brûlure
families.primary_effect: sensitivity recovery and some healing penalties

potion.example_valid_state: 75% HP + sprain -> potion use is valid and tactically rational
potion.design_rule: Potion value comes from restoring body condition as well as HP, not only filling the health bar.

examples: bandage can suppress or reduce deep-wound bleeding

body_system_integration.injury_progression: normal impact -> persistent trauma -> severe fracture/lesion -> possible mutilation when attack and target rules permit

death_interaction.death_is_not_a_rational_healing_method: Run loss equipment abandonment and evolving corpse risk remain substantial costs.

locked_rules: Trauma can occur while HP remains high.
Persistent injury families from LITD1 carry into LITD2.
A potion may be used regardless of current HP percentage.
The potion is the universal field cure for trauma.
HP healing does not automatically cure trauma.
Stabilization is not the same as cure.
Trauma state feeds gore body-zone and persistent-corpse systems.
